name: Omega-3 (EPA/DHA)
lead: Omega-3 fatty acids are polyunsaturated fats with a double bond three carbons from the methyl end of the chain. The three main types in human physiology are alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), found in some plants, and the long-chain eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), found in fish, fish oil and algae [1][2]. EPA and DHA are sold as fish-oil, krill-oil and algal-oil supplements and are also available as prescription omega-3 acid ethyl esters [1][3].

In appearance and skin contexts they are discussed for inflammatory skin conditions, dryness and general skin health, and in the wider supplement culture for recovery, mood and anti-inflammatory support [4][5]. The best-established regulatory use of purified EPA and DHA is lowering triglycerides in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia, as stated on the US label for omega-3 acid ethyl esters [3]. Wikipedia reports that supplementation has limited evidence of benefit for preventing cancer, all-cause mortality and most cardiovascular outcomes [1].

Trials of EPA and DHA for skin outcomes are few and mixed. The proposed mechanism is incorporation into cell membranes and conversion to specialised pro-resolving mediators such as resolvins and protectins that help end inflammation [6][7].

paras: Omega-3 intake is discussed for inflammatory skin conditions such as atopic dermatitis. A 2024 randomised trial tested fish-oil omega-3 combined with gamma-linolenic acid from blackcurrant seed oil in children with atopic dermatitis, and the paper notes that earlier studies of omega-3 in dermatitis have given mixed results [4]. A registered immunonutrition trial listed on ClinicalTrials.gov examined an omega-3-based approach to skin cancer prevention [8].

The US label for prescription omega-3 acid ethyl esters lists severe hypertriglyceridemia as its indication [3]. Meta-analyses have examined omega-3 in ADHD in youths (small but significant symptom improvement), diabetes markers (reductions in fasting glucose and insulin resistance but not HbA1c), and with resistance training for muscle strength [9][10][11][12]. A trial combined a Mediterranean-style diet with fish oil in people with depression, and others studied older adults' working memory, prostate cancer and endometriosis [13][14][15][16].

For skin, a 2024 randomised trial in children with atopic dermatitis tested omega-3 with GLA [4]. No large trial specifically testing EPA or DHA for cosmetic outcomes such as wrinkles or skin texture was identified in the available literature; the proposed anti-inflammatory mechanism is supported mainly by laboratory work and reviews [6][7][17].

Elsewhere the evidence base is large. A 2002 American Heart Association statement reviewed fish consumption, fish oil and cardiovascular disease [18]. Meta-analyses report a small effect on ADHD symptom scores in children (10 trials, 699 children in one analysis) and, in one 2022 review of 30 studies, reductions in fasting glucose and insulin resistance without a significant HbA1c effect [9][10][11]. A 2024 meta-analysis of four studies found that omega-3 plus resistance training improved muscle strength but not muscle mass in the pooled data [12]. A review of anti-inflammatory diets in rheumatoid arthritis rated its evidence very low [19].
Registered trials include studies in type 2 diabetes, perioperative gastric cancer, muscle wasting and phospholipid versus conventional omega-3 formulations [20][21][22][23].

The US label for omega-3 acid ethyl esters lists belching, dyspepsia and altered taste as the most common reactions, and warns of possible LDL cholesterol increases, caution with fish or shellfish hypersensitivity, liver enzyme monitoring in hepatic impairment and a possible association with more frequent recurrence of symptomatic atrial fibrillation or flutter in people with prior atrial fibrillation [3]. Pregnancy data are described as insufficient to identify a drug-associated risk [3]. A 2026 retrospective screening reported co-exposure to organohalogen contaminants through some fish oil supplements purchased in 2014 to 2017 [24].

Animals cannot make ALA and can convert it to EPA and then DHA only to a limited extent, which may decline with age [1]. EPA and DHA are incorporated into membranes and are precursors of resolvins, protectins and maresins, grouped as specialised pro-resolving mediators that have been studied for roles in ending inflammation [6][7]. A 2010 paper identified GPR120 as an omega-3 receptor with anti-inflammatory and insulin-sensitising effects in cells [25]. The prescription label says the triglyceride-lowering mechanism is not completely understood and may involve reduced hepatic triglyceride synthesis [3].

In 1929 George and Mildred Burr showed that fatty acids were essential nutrients and coined the term essential fatty acids [1]. In 2004 the US FDA granted a qualified health claim that supportive but not conclusive research suggests EPA and DHA may reduce coronary heart disease risk; Canada permits a claim about DHA and brain, eye and nerve development in young children [1]. Interest in the omega-6 to omega-3 ratio in Western diets has also been discussed in the literature [26].

lore.intro: On T Nation, omega-3 and fish oil are often presented, in forum posts and staff articles, as a foundational anti-inflammatory supplement, with threads on DHA for men, mood, sleep and timing [27][28][29][30][31].

claims.claim: Fish oil is a first-line anti-inflammatory supplement
claims.believers: T Nation articles state that inflammation underlies many unwanted conditions and that EPA and DHA from fish oil are the inflammation-fighting components, listing it among the first supplements to take [28][30].
claims.experts: Reviews describe pro-resolving mediators derived from EPA and DHA, but Wikipedia notes limited evidence for preventing most cardiovascular outcomes, cancer and all-cause mortality, and a review of anti-inflammatory diets in arthritis rated evidence very low [1][6][19].

claims.claim: Men need extra DHA because testosterone lowers DHA levels
claims.believers: A T Nation piece titled for "the manly omega-3" says testosterone lowers DHA levels and that most fish oils short-change men on DHA [32].
claims.experts: No trial identified in the available literature tested a DHA-specific supplement for men on this premise.

claims.claim: High-dose DHA reduces sleep apnea events
claims.believers: A forum poster reports lowering apneas from 48 to 17 per hour using high doses of omega-3 DHA and links a PubMed paper on membrane DHA [33].
claims.experts: This is an individual report; no randomised trial in the available literature confirms the result.

claims.believers: A T Nation article calls omega-3 a science-backed natural way to reduce anxiety, framing the issue as a basic deficiency [31].
claims.experts: Meta-analyses of other mental-health outcomes exist, for example modest ADHD symptom benefits in youths, while trials in depression pair fish oil with diet changes [9][13].

claims.claim: Omega-3 supports healthy telomeres and skin ageing
claims.believers: A T Nation article says inflammation is a main predator of telomeres and lists omega-3 among supplements to counter it [34].
claims.experts: Skin-specific trials are few; no study in the available literature shows omega-3 supplementation slowing visible skin ageing.
